column1: # Reference recordings, never committed: tools/fetch_references.py fetches each into a local
# cache and schrodr-reference-extract measures it. Columns: id, instrument, MIDI key (the note
# that sounds), dynamic, SOURCE:PATH (the sources are listed, with their pins, in
# tools/fetch_references.py), sha256, and the true sample rate where the file's header is wrong
# (else -). Sources: University of Iowa Musical Instrument Samples (Lawrence Fritts, "may be
# downloaded and used for any projects, without restrictions"); VSCO-2 CE and VCSL (CC0);
# Sonatina Symphonic Orchestra (CC0); jRhodes3d; the University of Edinburgh's DataShare;
# The 2012 Iowa viola files say 44.1 kHz but every note in them sounds 0.459 (44100/96000) of its
# name, its fundamental A4 at 202.9 Hz and G3 at 90.1 Hz: they are the 96 kHz takes.
# The Edinburgh clavichord is pitched at A = 415: a file named C4 sounds B3 and is keyed 59. Its
# names' second and third fields are an automatic pitch detector's guesses, often wrong. The
# noise-reduced takes are used (the others stand under 25 dB over the museum's air conditioning),
# and only those holding one note at the pitch their name says.
# The VCSL and VSCO note names put middle C at C3 (VCSL) and C4 (VSCO); the keys were checked by
# measurement. The organ rows are the Renaissance organ's stopped 8' (odd harmonics strong).
# The toy piano's lowest file, freesound 70718, sounds 355 Hz: F4 29 cents sharp, keyed 65.
# Celesta "soft" and "hard" are marked mf and ff; jRhodes3d's velocity layers 1, 3 and 5 pp, mf
# and ff (neither instrument's dynamics is judged).
# Left out because the note stands less than 25 dB over the recording's noise floor: upright C3
# and C7 at pp, the organ's C2, and (quiet takes over the 16-bit chain's floor) grand_C7_pp, violin_G3_pp, violin_G3_mf, violin_B3_pp,
# violin_E5_pp, viola_C3_pp, viola_E3_pp, viola_G3_pp, viola_A4_pp, glockenspiel_C6_pp,
# Left out: the celesta's E7 (it sounds 41 cents sharp) and G#7 (not found within 40 cents of
# its key). Left out because it is another note: Piano.ff.B0.aiff sounds C1, its partials on F = 32.40 Hz
# with B = 2.63e-4 exactly as Piano.ff.C1.aiff's (B0 is 30.87 Hz; the pp and mf B0 read 30.64).
